'''Anna Seelig-Löffler''' (born October 7, 1944 from [[Basel]]) is a [[Switzerland|Swiss]] [[biophysical chemist]] who worked at the [[Biozentrum University of Basel|Biozentrum]] [[University of Basel]], Switzerland.

==Life==
Anna Seelig-Löffler studied [[medicine]] and [[chemistry]] and received her PhD in [[physical chemistry]] from the University of Basel. As a postdoc she worked with Prof. [[Joachim Seelig]]. She then became an independent scientist in the Division of Biophysical Chemistry at the Biozentrum, habilitated in 1992, and later became honorary Professor of Biophysical Chemistry at the University of Basel. She reached emeritus status in 2012.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/emeriti-former-professors/emeriti/anna-seelig-loeffler |title=Prof. Dr. Anna Seelig-Löffler, Titular Professor Emerita |publisher=biozentrum.unibas.ch|date= |accessdate=2022-02-09}}</ref>

==Work==
Her areas of expertise include the structural and functional analysis of [[Biological membrane|membrane]]s and their [[lipid]] and [[protein]] components.<ref>{{cite journal | pmid =16877510 | volume=91 | issue=8 | pages=2943–55 | title=Interaction of verapamil with lipid membranes and P-glycoprotein: connecting thermodynamics and membrane structure with functional activity. | date=15 October 2006 | journal=Biophys. J. | doi=10.1529/biophysj.106.089581 | last1=Meier | first1=M | last2=Li-Blatter | first2=Xiaochun | last3=Seelig | first3=Joachim | last4=Seelig | first4=Anna| doi-access=free | pmc=1578493 }}</ref> More recently her work focused on [[ATP Binding Cassette]] (ABC)<ref>{{cite journal | pmid =37070101 | volume=6 | issue=1 | pages=1–29 | title=P-glycoprotein (ABCB1) - weak dipolar interactions provide the key to understanding allocrite recognition, binding, and transport. | date=1 January 2023 | journal=Cancer Drug Resist. | doi=10.20517/cdr.2022.59 | last1=Seelig | first1=Anna | last2=Li-Blatter | first2=Xiaochun| doi-access=free | pmc=10105259 }}</ref> transporters, such as [[P-glycoprotein]], which prevent drug uptake across cell membranes and cause [[multidrug resistance]]. She discovered a universal substrate pattern for P-glycoprotein which made it possible to estimate the chance of a substrate to reach its target site.<ref>{{cite journal | pmid =9492291 | volume=251 | issue=1–2 | pages=252–61 | title=A general pattern for substrate recognition by P-glycoprotein. | date=15 January 1998 | journal=Eur J Biochem | doi=10.1046/j.1432-1327.1998.2510252.x | last1=Seelig | first1=Anna }}</ref> Based on these findings she developed a model to predict drug uptake across biological membranes.<ref>{{cite journal | pmid =27977215 | volume=14 | issue=1 | pages=284–295 | title=31 P and 1 H NMR Studies of the Molecular Organization of Lipids in the Parallel Artificial Membrane Permeability Assay | date=2017-01-03 | journal=Mol Pharm | doi=10.1021/acs.molpharmaceut.6b00889 | last1=Assmus | first1=Frauke | last2=Ross | first2=Alfred | last3=Fischer | first3=Holger | last4=Seelig | first4=Joachim | last5=Seelig | first5=Anna }}</ref>
